title: Geo-tier escalation: model-version affinity and canary stickiness semantics
creator: Priya Kapoor
description:
Problem: We need clear, deterministic semantics when multiple routing controls overlap: region preference, customer tier, per-request model version pin, and active rollout policies (canary / A-B). Current behavior is nondeterministic under load: pinned requests sometimes bypass canary rules, sticky affinity can flip when route capacities are rebalanced, and fallbacks to quantized or smaller variants are inconsistent across regions.

Goal: Define and implement a route-resolution algorithm and configuration model that: (1) preserves model-version pin semantics for customer-pinned requests while still allowing safe canary exposure where intended; (2) provides a predictable, observable degrade path when capacity or compatibility constraints occur; (3) supports sticky affinity for session-level canary exposure with configurable TTL and eviction rules; (4) encodes geo + tier escalation rules (region preferred -> tier fallback -> global) with explicit prioritization and time windows.

This ticket scopes the resolver design, API flags, and a working prototype with unit + integration tests and telemetry hooks. Implementation will land as a new resolver module behind a feature flag so we can A/B test rollout behavior internally before enabling for customers.
acceptance_criteria: Deterministic routing precedence documented and implemented: region selection -> tier policy -> request-level pin -> rollout affinity -> degrade/fallback policy.

Pinned requests that explicitly specify a model version always route to that version unless a hard incompatibility (e.g., model architecture mismatch) is detected; in that case return 409 with structured error and suggested fallback variants.
Canary exposure via sticky affinity works for session-scoped keys: TTL configurable per-route (default 10m) and metrics emitted when affinity is assigned/evicted.

When capacity is constrained, the resolver escalates: try preferred region/tier -> alternative tier in same region -> alternate region -> fallback model variants (quantized/last-stable) according to policy order.
All decisions are annotated in trace/span metadata and appear in routing dashboard for sampling (route.reason, route.path, route.affinity).
Feature gated behind runtime-1.23 flag and rolled out to internal canary cohort with no customer-facing config changes by default.
recent_updates: 2026-03-10: Initial spec written; scoped to resolver + telemetry. Linked parent issue ENG-34102.
2026-03-11: Prototype resolver implemented (PR 4123) that enforces precedence and emits route.reason tags. Basic unit tests added.
2026-03-12: Design review with PM: agreed on TTL defaults and that explicit model pin should be honored unless incompatible. PM asked for error payload shape for pin failures.
2026-03-12: Discovered edge case when pinned user token has stale affinity mapping pointing to decommissioned canary variant — added eviction semantics to next steps.
review_feedback: Alice Chen (PM): request-level pin must be explicit in API shape; reject silent overrides. Add clear customer-facing error code and docs for fallback suggestions.
Jared Lin (SRE): emit an alert if >1% of pinned requests are receiving fallback variants for more than 5m — indicates rollout misconfiguration.
Leah Park (DevX): expose a small SDK helper that surface route.reason in debug logs for customers on Dedicated tier.
next_steps: Complete PR 4123: add structured 409 error payload and suggested_variant list.
Add integration test that simulates: pinned request + canary active + capacity pressure, assert correct error/fallback path.
Wire telemetry: distribute route.reason tag to tracing and emit routing_counts by region/tier/variant.
Stage feature-flagged rollout to internal org + two opt-in customers, run 2-week canary and evaluate metrics (latency P95, fallback ratio, pin-failure-rate).
Update API docs with pinning semantics and example error payloads.
notes: Trade-offs discussed: honoring explicit pins preserves customer expectations but increases risk of capacity hot-spots in the pinned variant. To mitigate, we will add quota protections and a configurable hard-fail vs soft-fail policy per customer. Also considering an 'allow-pin-downgrade' flag for customers that prefer automatic compatible fallback when pinned variant is unavailable. Need legal/cust-ops signoff for any change that might silently override a customer pin.
